experiments.title: Raise the water
experiments.instruction: Predict first. Set the surface to 1 m in the narrow tank with the outlet fixed at 0.5 m, then change only the surface to 2 m.
experiments.observe: Head rises from 0.5 to 1.5 m. Calculated gauge pressure and net force on the fixed wall sensor triple, while ideal speed rises by √3. Explain why pressure and speed respond by different factors.

experiments.title: Change tank shape
experiments.instruction: Predict first. Keep the surface at 2 m and outlet at 0.5 m, then change only the tank from narrow to wide. Compare one instant before either tank drains.
experiments.observe: Volume rises from 2,000 to 6,480 L, but head stays 1.5 m. Wall-sensor gauge pressure, sensor net force and ideal speed remain unchanged. Explain why volume alone does not set pressure at that depth.
